text.p: An Eritrean government commission said on Monday it nationalised 174 houses that were built with public money by Ethiopia's Dergue military junta before its overthrow in 1991.

Yemane Dawit, an associate commissioner with the land and housing commission, said 80 percent of the 174 houses in the Eritrean capital Asmara ordered nationalised on January 27 were owned by former Dergue officials and their collaborators.

Eritrea became independent from Ethiopia in 1993. The government says it has returned 59,000 houses to the people who owned them before the houses were nationalised by the then Marxist rulers in 1976.
